Yesterday at a #UNGA80 side event on Data, Digital Transformation and the Resilience in the Energy Transition, I discussed a defining question for the AI era:
 
AI is already reshaping the #energy transition - but does it build resilience, or deepen fragility?
 
Last year, in Mexico’s drought-stricken Querétaro region, farmers rationed water and lost crops. Just a few kilometers away, billions were invested in new AI data centers requiring extensive water cooling systems. The paradox is striking.
 
By 2027, data centers are projected to consume nearly 900 TWh of electricity and 6.6 billion cubic meters of water annually, largely driven by AI. But at the same time, AI also holds promise: it can optimize renewable grids, enable faster climate forecasting, and unlock billions in private finance for clean energy in the Global South.
 
During the discussion, youth delegates asked powerful questions:
👉 Are we using #AI in a way that advances sustainable energy for all?
👉 How can we prevent AI from becoming another burden on already stressed systems, and instead ensure it can create real opportunities for development?
👉 Will we step up to govern our energy transitions, so they are not only resilient, but also just?
 
The answers will define whether AI accelerates the clean energy future - or becomes another burden on already fragile systems.
